resolutions.researcher_notes: Searched Raguba/Sirte Basin gas pipeline, NOC/Sirte Oil Company sources, Libya Herald/Observer/Ecofin/energycapitalpower for current status; no article names this exact 20-in Raguba/km-110 segment individually (it is a minor internal Sirte Oil trunk-network link, not a headline project). OPEC ASB 2012 Table 4.10 (opec.org PDF, live opec.org link is dead per known gotcha, recovered via Wayback snapshot 2012-08-02 + pdftotext) lists 'Raguba/km-110' as an active Sirte Oil gas line in its 2011 operating-pipelines table -- direct textual confirmation of status=operating for that year. Status is inferable, not literal, thereafter: no evidence anywhere of shut-in/decommissioning, and the broader Sirte Oil and Gas Production and Manufacturing Co. network of which this segment is a component part (Attahaddy/km-91.5, Km-81.5/Brega, Raguba/km-110, Sahel/km-81.5, Km-91.5/Brega all appear together in the same OPEC table as one interconnected corridor) is confirmed still actively operated and under active expansion as of March 2026 (Ecofin Agency, citing Libya Observer reporting: NOC/Sirte Oil and Gas Production and Manufacturing Co. bringing a new Farigh-Brega line online, tying into an 'existing 42-inch pipeline operated by' that same company in the Zueitina/km-91 area). Second source does not name Raguba/km-110 itself (contains_value=false for the literal segment) so treated as context corroboration of continued network operation, not a direct duplicate confirmation -- tier kept medium rather than high.

OPEC ASB 2012, Table 4.10 'Gas pipelines in OPEC Members, 2011' (p.75) lists the line 'Raguba/km-110, Owner: Sirte Oil' directly under the Libya gas-pipelines heading -- table title itself is the direct confirmation of Fuel=Gas (this is not the parallel oil-pipelines table, which lists a separate 'Raguba/Nasser-Al-Brayqah line' entry). No second, independently-sourced statement naming this exact segment as a gas line was found; the fuel type is unambiguous within the one strong source, so kept at medium rather than fabricating a second citation for an uncontested, narrow technical fact.

OPEC ASB 2012 Table 4.10 gives 'Raguba/km-110, Owner: Sirte Oil, Length 88 miles, Diameter 20 in, Capacity 3,964,882 (1,000 scm/yr)'. 3,964,882 thousand scm/yr = 3.964882 bcm/y, which rounds to the GEM value 3.96 bcm/y -- exact match. url_verifier's automated substring check FAILs on this PDF (200 but 'Raguba' not found) because the compressed PDF stream isn't text-extractable by a naive byte scan (the documented ligature/binary-PDF false-negative in url_verifier's own docstring); I confirmed the value manually via pdftotext extraction of the same Wayback snapshot, which cleanly shows the row. No second, independent numeric source for this specific segment's capacity was found despite extensive searching (Wikipedia, Libya Herald, Libya Observer, Ecofin, industry press, Arabic search all return only the general Raguba oil field / broader Sirte network, never this specific 20-in gas segment's throughput) -- single strong source, tier medium.

Same OPEC ASB 2012 Table 4.10 row: Length 88 miles = 141.62 km, which rounds to the GEM value 142.00 km -- exact match once mi->km converted. No second independent source with a length figure for this specific segment was found; single strong source, tier medium.
Same OPEC ASB 2012 Table 4.10 row: Diameter 20 inches -- exact match to GEM value 20.00 in. No second independent numeric source found for this exact segment; single strong source, tier medium.

OPEC ASB 2012 lists the line under the 'Libya (cont'd)' heading of Table 4.10. Wikipedia's Raguba field article independently confirms Raguba is an onshore field in Libya's Sirte Basin (Concession 20), operated by Sirte Oil Company, connected by pipeline to the Nasser-Brega main line -- two independent sources agreeing Libya is the correct start/end country for both endpoints (this is an onshore trunk segment within one field/network, not a border-crossing line).

OPEC ASB 2012 names 'Sirte Oil' as the owner/operator of the Raguba/km-110 line. Wikipedia's Sirte Oil Company article independently confirms SOC operates under, and was formed in 1981 as a subsidiary of, the state-owned National Oil Corporation (taking over former Esso/Exxon holdings) -- consistent with GEM's Owner1=Libyan National Oil Corp at 100%. Neither source states an explicit ownership percentage for SOC itself (state subsidiaries of NOC are conventionally treated as 100% NOC-owned in this tracker's existing entries), so kept at medium/inferred-percentage rather than high; no source suggests any other owner or a JV structure for this segment.
